Creating Our Future By Learning Together
Welcome
Choosing a school for your child is one of the most important decisions a parent can make. At St Katherine's School & Nursery, we are committed to providing an exciting and broad curriculum.
This allows our children to thrive academically and to develop the skills and understanding that they will need to be successful in the future. We recognise every child is unique and focus on their individual needs, within a vibrant, happy and safe environment, to ensure they reach their full potential.
St Katherine's School & Nursery has fantastic facilities: it is set on extensive grounds, with its own art studio, swimming pool, sensory rooms and a well-stocked library. These are fully utilised to enhance the learning experience of our children and allow them to excel and enjoy their learning.
We are extremely proud of our school, our children and staff. We take pride in ensuring that we are 'Creating our future by learning together.'
New Parent Open Days (Intake September 2027)

There will also be an opportunity to meet some of our School Governors and teachers, whilst our Year 6 children will take you for a tour around our learning environment, which includes classroom visits.

French
At St Katherine's School & Nursery we have chosen to study French due to Kent being 'The Gateway to Europe' and France being the closest neighbour.
In Early Years and Key Stage 1 children begin to use a few French words as greetings. Once children move into KS2 they follow sequences of lessons on Salut. In each year group children have an opportunity to build on their conversational skills and learn new vocabulary on different topics.

Religious Education
We use the Kent syllabus to plan our Religious Education lessons at St Katherine's School & Nursery. Children learn about the lives of Christians, Muslims, Hindus and Humanists. As they learn about different religions they consider their own beliefs and values. Children are taught significant stories from some religions and learn about traditions and beliefs.
We want children leaving us to understand and be respectful to others beliefs and feelings.

Maths
At St Katherine’s School and Nursery, we are passionate about mathematics and understand how important and valuable it is. Our mission is that regardless of where children start, in terms of their mathematical understanding, that they will maximise their academic achievement and leave our school with an appreciation and enthusiasm for maths, resulting in a lifelong positive relationship with number.
In order to ensure that all children can enjoy and achieve in mathematics, we follow a mastery approach supported by White Rose Maths materials. This means that we hold an expectation that all children will achieve a deep understanding of mathematical concepts and use this flexibly and with confidence. This mastery approach means that children spend more time learning about key mathematical concepts and are given time to build a deeper understanding. Learning is broken down into smaller steps for children to allow this and helps us to avoid gaps in children’s learning and address any existing gaps.
Problem solving sits at the heart of our mathematics provision and opportunities are given for children to calculate with confidence, explore mathematical structures, think strategically, work systematically, reason and explain their understanding and make conjectures.
Assessment is a key focus in all learning and within maths lessons allows teachers to ensure they are teaching the children what they need to know, when they need to know it. This means that children are able to build on prior knowledge and make progress with their learning. It also allows teachers to offer opportunities to deepen understanding and further support the development of mathematical understanding.

They are provided with opportunities to perform to an audience. In order to ensure there is clear progression and children develop skills we use Charanga to teach music.

Phonics & Reading
Phonics
At St Katherine's School & Nursery we follow the Sounds-Write Scheme.
Sounds-Write is an expertly structured synthetic phonics programme based on the science of reading. This multisensory, code-oriented, comprehensive approach to literacy has been designed by teachers— for teachers.
Our teachers and teacher assistants access a high-quality development programme which empowers them to impart on children those most critical abilities for a happy, successful life and career: excellent reading and writing skills.
Please see our teaching sequence for Reception to Year 2.
Reading
At St. Katherine’s School and Nursery, we believe reading is an essential life skill and lies at the heart of our curriculum. Every single class has daily phonics or reading sessions where we place a high importance in the ability to decode real words and become fluent readers. We do this by giving the children plenty of opportunities to hear model readers, time for repeated reading of texts and chances to read aloud with peers.
Our school reading spine is selected to provide a clear vision of our children’s reading diet and ensure coverage of a diverse range of authors and genres including; fiction, non-fiction and poetry. Using carefully selected texts, children are able to build on their knowledge of the curriculum as well as develop a stronger understanding of relevant vocabulary. With the understanding that greater word recognition and fluency allows children to develop deeper comprehension skills. We feel it is also important, through Key Stage 2 that we allocate time to learn Etymological/Tier 2 vocabulary too.
Reading For Pleasure
In or school we want to build a community of readers who love reading and create a positive reading culture. We are fostering our love of reading in a number of ways:
Weekly visits to our recently updated and well-stocked library
Promoting love of books within the school - termly Reading Newsletters, Book Fairs, Book Swaps
Year 6 Reading Ambassadors
Rewarding daily reading through our 'Race to Read'
Daily class book read by our teachers in every class
Encouraging a varied diet of genres and authors through St. Katherine’s Reading Spine

SEND (Special Educational Needs & Disability)
St Katherine’s School & Nursery SEN Information for Parents and Carers
We are committed to:
What are special needs?
Special educational needs could mean that a child has:
Children make progress at different rates and have different ways in which they learn best. Teachers take account of this in the way they organise their lessons and teach. Children making slower progress or having particular difficulties in one area may be given extra help to help them succeed.
Identifying Children’s Additional Needs
At St. Katherine’s School & Nursery we monitor the progress of all children six times a year to review their academic, social and emotional progress.
We also use a range of assessments with all the children at various points, such as:
Where progress is not sufficient, even if a special educational need has not been identified, we develop a plan to allow the child to catch up. This may mean adapting classroom practise or providing extra support in the form of small group work or 1:1 support.
Some children may continue to make inadequate progress, despite high-quality teaching targeted at their areas of weakness. For these children, and in consultation with parents, we will use a range of assessment tools or access support and advice from outside agencies to determine the cause of the learning difficulty. The purpose of this more detailed assessment is to understand what additional resources and different approaches are required to enable the pupil to make better progress. These will be shared with parents, put into a SEN support plan and reviewed regularly, and refined/revised if necessary. At this point we will have identified that the child has a special educational need because the school is making special educational provision for the child which is additional and different to what is normally available.
If the child is able to make good progress using this additional and different resource (but would not be able to maintain this good progress without it) we will continue to identify the child as having a special educational need. If the child is able to maintain good progress without the additional and different resources, he or she will not be identified with special educational needs. When any change in identification of SEN is made, parents will be notified.
We will ensure that all teachers and support staff who work with the child are aware of the support to be provided and the teaching approaches to be used.

Access Arrangements & Equal Opportunities for SEN Children
At St Katherine’s School & Nursery we aim to create an inclusive culture for all staff, children, families and visitors to the school. We recognise, respect and value people’s differences and ensure that individuals or groups of individuals are treated equally; including ability, disability, race, gender, belief, sexual orientation and age.
We promote equality and diversity treating all staff and children fairly ensuring equal access to opportunities to enable children and staff to fully participate in the learning process and achieve and equip them with the skills to challenge inequality and discrimination.
The school environment includes designated parking and step free access to the school building. There are designated disabled toilets and grab rails around the school so that children can develop independence in self-care skills.
Please click here for further information on Equality
Who should I contact if I have any questions or concerns about my child’s SEND?
In the first instance you should always speak to your child's class teacher, and then they may advise you to speak to our SENCO Mrs Caroline Loveland
Email: cloveland@st-katherines.kent.sch.uk

Art & Design
At St Katherine's School & Nursery we value children’s creativity, individuality and the development of artistic skills.
All children have the opportunity to develop a variety of artistic techniques and skills, and build upon these as they progress through the school. All the Art units begin with a focus on an artist to enable children to develop their understanding and knowledge of famous artists. Throughout units of work, they may also visit and look at other artists to broaden their understanding of how artists work linking and building on each other.
We use sketch books to enable children to showcase their learning in the most amazing way. Each child receives their own personal sketchbook, and it is there for them to express themselves and their learning.

Computing
At St Katherine's School & Nursery we use Purple Mash for computing. Children all have their own log in details and can access their learning at home and school. The curriculum includes computer science, information technology and digital literacy in all year groups.
In computer science the children learn about algorithms and programming and develop their skills as they give instructions and debug programs with increasing complexity.
In information technology children learn to search for information and present data and information in a variety of ways using a range of software.
Digital literacy is increasingly important in today’s society, children learn how to use technology safely and with respect. Children in all year groups cover digital literacy every term.
Children have access to class sets of laptops and Ipads for their learning.

Geography
At St Katherine’s School & Nursery we follow the Pearson Geography Scheme. All children from Years 1 to 6 will complete 3 terms of Geography each year, during these terms 1 hour of Geography will be taught each week. The topics covered are carefully sequenced to ensure children have opportunities to revisit ideas and issues and deepen their understanding.
In Key Stage 1 children will begin by learning about similarities and differences between the countries of the UK, they will consider landscape, transport, weather and settlements. They will also begin to consider some environmental issues and consider sustainability. As children move into Key Stage 2 they will look at populations and settlements around the world and look more at the impact of humans on the environment.
All children are supported in accessing the Geography curriculum regardless of their needs.

History
At St Katherine’s School & Nursery we are following the Pearson History Scheme. All children from Years 1 to 6 will complete 3 terms of History each year, during these terms 1 hour of History will be taught each week. The topics covered are carefully sequenced to ensure children have opportunities to revisit ideas and issues and deepen their understanding as well as developing a sense of chronology.
While in Key Stage 1 children will learn about events and people in History such as The Great Fire of London and the life of Pocahontas, they will also learn about developments in travel and transport. In Key Stage 2 children will learn about ancient civilisations from the Shang Dynasty to Ancient Greece and the Benin Kingdom. They will also learn about the Industrial Revolution, civil rights and changes in Britain.
All children are supported in accessing the History curriculum regardless of their needs.

PSHE
The PSHE curriculum at St Katherine’s School & Nursery is from PSHE association’s curriculum builders as recommended by the Department of Education. To deliver these lessons, we use a range of resources, such as visits, speakers, organisations, charities and KAPOW.
Our themes are split into three main categories: Relationships, Living in the Wider World and Health and wellbeing. The children use a spiral curriculum, and they build upon their learning year by year.
PSHE education gives children at St Katherine’s the opportunity to learn about their and others mental health and wellbeing, and teaches some ways to manage our mental health and recognise poor mental health. PSHE education helps children and young people to achieve their potential by supporting their wellbeing and tackling issues that can affect their ability to learn, such as anxiety and unhealthy relationships. Children are given the opportunity to recognise different feelings and discuss when we might feel them, with the aim of reducing the stigma around mental health, and allowing the children to understand that everyone has mental health, and there are people who will support us when we need it.
The social, emotional and mental health needs of all children underpin all teaching and interactions at St Katherine’s. All staff are aware of the children’s needs, and understand the importance of children’s positive mental health and wellbeing, and its impact on their education. At St Katherine’s, we strive to develop and foster an inclusive and supportive environment always, and this is ensured through our PSHE education curriculum.
Children in EYFS develop skills that form a crucial foundation for later teaching of PSHE/Relationship at KS1. Both curriculums complement each other, providing opportunities for progression throughout the school. The PSHE curriculum in EYFS is largely covered in the following areas: Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSED) and Understanding the World (UTW).
